chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan who said:

I asked him (asws) about three who entered into the Tawaaf. So one of them said to his companion, 'Memorise the Tawaaf (count)'. So when they thought that they had finished, one said, 'With me there are six circuits'. He (asws) said: 'If all of them doubt, let them resume (start over); and if they do not doubt, and each one of them knows what is in his hand (count), let them build (upon their count)'.

key_terms.أَشْوَاط: Ashwat (singular: shawt, meaning circuits or rounds)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for Tawaaf when a group is unsure about the number of circuits completed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'building upon certainty' (al-bina' ala al-sahih) in communal worship, distinguishing between shared doubt requiring a full restart and individual certainty allowing for partial completion. It highlights the Shia juristic preference for ease and validity over excessive caution when individual knowledge is preserved, reflecting the broader Usuli approach to ritual purity and prayer.
